paper_title: Feedback Friction LLMs Struggle to Fully Incorporate External Feedback
caption: : TriviaQA confidence vs. accuracy
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the relationship between initial confidence and accuracy in the TriviaQA dataset, showing three distinct metrics: Final Accuracy, Δ Accuracy, and Initial Accuracy. The x-axis represents Initial Confidence, ranging from approximately 0.71 to 1.00, with tick marks at regular intervals (e.g., 0.71, 0.73, 0.79, 0.82, 0.83, 0.85, 0.86, 0.87, 0.90, 0.91, 0.93, 0.94, 0.96, 0.97, 0.98, 0.99, 1.00), and is scaled linearly. The y-axis represents Accuracy, ranging from 0.0 to 1.0, also linearly scaled, with tick marks at 0.0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8, and 1.0. The blue solid line with circular markers and error bars represents Final Accuracy, which starts at approximately 0.9 at an initial confidence of 0.71, dips to around 0.7 at 0.73, rises to 1.0 at 0.79, then fluctuates between 0.8 and 1.0 across higher confidence values. The green dashed line with square markers and error bars represents Initial Accuracy, beginning near 0.5 at 0.71, rising to approximately 0.9 at 0.79, then declining to around 0.4 at 0.87, and showing further fluctuations, reaching about 0.8 at 1.00. The orange dash-dotted line with diamond markers and error bars represents Δ Accuracy, starting at approximately 0.35 at 0.71, dropping to around 0.1 at 0.73, remaining low until 0.85, then rising to about 0.4 at 0.90, before declining again to nearly 0.0 at 1.00. All lines include error bars indicating variability, with the largest error bars observed for Initial Accuracy at lower confidence values.
